item.title: “The mind is fickle and restless, Hard to guard, hard to restrain. The wise make it straight, Like a fletcher straightens an arrow.” “Like a…
item.description:
“The mind is fickle and restless,
Hard to guard, hard to restrain.
The wise make it straight,
Like a fletcher straightens an arrow.”

“Like a fish thrown on dry ground,
Wrenched from its watery home,
This mind struggles and thrashes
To escape Māra’s grip.”

“Hard to hold, fickle,
It jumps where it wishes.
Good is it to tame the mind —
A tamed mind brings happiness.”

“The mind is hard to see, subtle,
It jumps where it wishes.
The wise guard the mind —
A guarded mind brings happiness.”

From: Dhammapada 33-43

item.title: Elder Nandaka: Foul is the thing! Full of foul smell and stench, Possessed by Māra, Oozing many streams — This body has nine streams, Always…
item.description:
Elder Nandaka:

Foul is the thing!
Full of foul smell and stench,
Possessed by Māra,
Oozing many streams —
This body has nine streams,
Always flowing.

Do not despise the ancients!
Do not insult the Tathāgata!
They do not long for the heavenly realm,
Let alone the human world.

The fool, without wisdom,
With evil intent, enveloped by delusion —
That one, full of lust,
Is caught in Māra’s snare.

Those who have escaped
Greed, hatred, and delusion —
They are not lustful,
The snare is cut, they are unbound.

From: Theragāthā 4.4
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Householder, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. If a monk delights in those forms,…
item.description:
“Householder, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. If a monk delights in those forms, praises them, and dwells with lust for them, depending on them, consciousness arises with clinging to them. Householder, a monk who has clinging does not attain complete Nibbāna … Households, there are tastes cognizable by the tongue … Householder, there are phenomena cognizable by the mind that are desirable … enticing. If a monk delights in those phenomena, praises them, and dwells with lust for them — because he delights, praises, and dwells with lust, depending on them, consciousness arises with clinging to them. Having clinging, householder, that monk does not attain Nibbāna. This, householder, is the cause, this is the reason why some beings here and now do not attain complete Nibbāna.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.124

item.title: “Monks, there are these three ways that sensual desire arises. What three? Sensual desire for present objects, delight in one’s own creations, and acceptance of…
item.description:
“Monks, there are these three ways that sensual desire arises. What three? Sensual desire for present objects, delight in one’s own creations, and acceptance of what is created by others. These, monks, are the three ways that sensual desire arises.

The gods who enjoy sense pleasures,
The gods of great power,
The gods who delight in creation,
And the gods who wield power over others —
Enjoying sense pleasures,
Here and there in various existences,
They do not go beyond the wandering.

Knowing this peril,
The wise should abandon all sensual desires,
Whether divine or human,
Here and in future states.

Those who have cut the stream
So hard to cross,
Who have broken the bond
To what is dear and beautiful,
Having made an end of suffering,
Without remainder,
Those noble ones who have seen,
The wise with knowledge,
Having rightly known the destruction of birth,
Do not go to renewed existence.”

From: Itivuttaka 95

item.title: “The stream of craving flows everywhere, The creeper of craving sprouts and stands. Seeing that creeper that has arisen, Cut its root with wisdom.” “People,…
item.description:
“The stream of craving flows everywhere,
The creeper of craving sprouts and stands.
Seeing that creeper that has arisen,
Cut its root with wisdom.”

“People, immersed in sensual pleasures,
Delight in various pleasures.
Though they seek happiness,
They undergo birth and aging.”

“People bound by craving,
Thrashing about, terrified,
Like hares caught in a snare —
Bound by craving,
They undergo suffering for a long time.”

“People bound by craving,
Thrashing about, terrified,
Like hares caught in a snare —
Therefore, a monk who desires his own dispassion
Should abandon craving.”

From: Dhammapada 334-359

item.title: - “Venerable sir, how did you cross the flood?” - “Friend, by not halting and not straining, I crossed the flood.” - “But how, venerable…
item.description:
- “Venerable sir, how did you cross the flood?”
- “Friend, by not halting and not straining, I crossed the flood.”
- “But how, venerable sir, did you cross the flood by not halting and not straining?”
- “When I halted, friend, I sank. When I strained, I was swept away. So, friend, by not halting and not straining, I crossed the flood.”
(The deity):
After a long time I see
A brahmin who is fully extinguished —
By not halting, not straining,
He has crossed all clinging in the world.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.1
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: Like a newly decorated medicine box, This foul body is adorned for the occasion — Enough to fool a fool, But not one who seeks…
item.description:
Like a newly decorated medicine box,
This foul body is adorned for the occasion —
Enough to fool a fool,
But not one who seeks the far shore.

The hunter set his trap and snare,
The wise deer does not approach,
Having eaten the crops, we go our way,
Leaving the trapper to lament.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 82 – Raṭṭhapālasutta

item.title: “I do not see any other thing, monks, that leads to such great benefit as heedfulness. Heedfulness, monks, leads to great benefit.”
item.description:
“I do not see any other thing, monks, that leads to such great benefit as heedfulness. Heedfulness, monks, leads to great benefit.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 1.83

item.title: “Form, monks, is suffering. Whatever cause and condition for the arising of form — that too is suffering. Form that has arisen from suffering, monks,…
item.description:
“Form, monks, is suffering. Whatever cause and condition for the arising of form — that too is suffering. Form that has arisen from suffering, monks, how could it be happiness? Feeling … Perception … Formations … Consciousness is suffering. Whatever cause and condition for the arising of consciousness — that too is suffering. Consciousness that has arisen from suffering, monks, how could it be happiness? Seeing thus, monks, a well-taught noble disciple becomes disenchanted with form … disenchanted with feeling … disenchanted with perception … disenchanted with formations … disenchanted with consciousness. Being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate … He knows: ‘… there is no more of this state of being.’”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.19
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Poṭṭhapāda, when defiling states are eliminated, pure states increase; here and now, by direct knowledge, one realizes and abides in fully developed, vast wisdom. Then…
item.description:
“Poṭṭhapāda, when defiling states are eliminated, pure states increase; here and now, by direct knowledge, one realizes and abides in fully developed, vast wisdom. Then joy arises, gladness, tranquility, mindfulness, clear comprehension, and a pleasant abiding arise.”

From: Dīgha Nikāya 9 – Poṭṭhapādasutta
